title: Event marketing: pick the right events, then win in the before and after
summary: Corey's events playbook argues that results come from selecting the right events and running the before-and-after arc well, not from the event itself. It covers the four roles (host, sponsor, speak, attend), the content arc, and a measurement ladder built on cost per qualified meeting rather than badge scans.

principles.text: Selection beats execution: events are the costliest, riskiest channel, so choose them carefully.
principles.quote: events are the most expensive, riskiest, hardest-to-measure channel — the leverage is in **selection**, not execution.

principles.text: The event is a small part of event marketing; pipeline is made before and won or lost after.
principles.quote: The event itself is the smallest part of event marketing. Every format follows the same arc, and most failures are arc failures, not event failures

principles.text: Book meetings before you arrive instead of hoping for hallway encounters.
principles.quote: A meeting booked two weeks out is worth ten hopeful hallway collisions.

principles.text: Bigger conferences aren't better; niche events often win on qualified leads per dollar.
principles.quote: Mega-conferences mean more noise, higher cost, and audience dilution (students, press, vendors, tourists). Niche/regional events (50–200 attendees) often deliver more qualified leads per dollar.

principles.text: The topic is the targeting: pick subjects your buyer would attend even if they never buy.
principles.quote: "State of [category] 2026" attracts your ICP; "All about [your product]" attracts existing customers only.

principles.text: Track pipeline metrics, not vanity ones; a badge scan is not a lead.
principles.quote: A scan is a person who walked slowly. Qualify before it enters the pipeline.
